variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Data quality filtering is a versioned decision process that separates records eligible for an ML dataset from records that must be quarantined or excluded. A filter can validate structure and provenance, detect duplicates, apply learned quality or safety models, and route uncertain cases to human review.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Define the release contract before choosing filters”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Contract gates
pairs.detail: Check decoding, schema, length bounds, required metadata, source eligibility, and parser success.
pairs.explanation: Check decoding, schema, length bounds, required metadata, source eligibility, and parser success. Failures should be reproducible from the same bytes and policy.

pairs.label: Redundancy gates
pairs.detail: Remove exact or near duplicates with a declared unit, normalization, similarity method, cluster policy, and protected exceptions.
pairs.explanation: Remove exact or near duplicates with a declared unit, normalization, similarity method, cluster policy, and protected exceptions.

pairs.label: Learned gates
pairs.detail: Use model scores for bounded decisions such as relevance, content quality, or safety.
pairs.explanation: Use model scores for bounded decisions such as relevance, content quality, or safety. Treat thresholds and model versions as release inputs.

pairs.label: Human review
pairs.detail: Review samples and ambiguous cases under written guidance.
pairs.explanation: Review samples and ambiguous cases under written guidance. Track disagreement and adjudication rather than treating one label as ground truth.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is: every published or quarantined record must be explainable by the source snapshot, policy version, gate versions, and reason codes that produced the decision.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Contract gates: Check decoding, schema, length bounds, required metadata, source eligibility, and parser success. Redundancy gates: Remove exact or near duplicates with a declared unit, normalization, similarity method, cluster policy, and protected exceptions. Learned gates: Use model scores for bounded decisions such as relevance, content quality, or safety. Human review: Review samples and ambiguous cases under written guidance.

variants.prompt: What is the safest default disposition when a record has an unknown license or broken provenance?
options: Publish it because the text looks useful
Quarantine it with a reason code until policy resolves the uncertainty
Delete the source metadata and continue
Assign the average license of the rest of the corpus
variants.explanation: Unknown eligibility is not evidence of permission. Quarantine preserves the record and decision context without silently publishing it.
optionFeedback: Unknown eligibility is not evidence of permission. Quarantine preserves the record and decision context without silently publishing it.

variants.prompt: In a deterministic early-exit cascade, why can gate order change CPU work without changing the final retained set?
options: Every record eventually passes all gates
A record rejected by any gate remains rejected, but an earlier failure avoids later calls
Later gates automatically become less accurate
The order changes every gate threshold
variants.explanation: When gate predicates are fixed, the union of failed records stays the same. Cheap, high-rejection gates can stop doomed records before expensive evaluation.

variants.prompt: A pass rate drops after the source mix changes. What should the operator do first?

Compare versioned source and slice distributions, then sample the changed decision reasons
Delete quarantined records
Assume the classifier degraded
variants.explanation: Pass-rate movement is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Source-mix, policy, schema, and model changes must be separated before thresholds are changed.
